explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-based GEMBA-MQM metric against human MQM judgments through correlation analysis and error detection performance, reporting quantitative metrics (Spearman correlation, F1 score) and analyzing preference bias.

prompts.notes: The paper only mentions that GEMBA-MQM is a GPT-4-based quality estimation metric, but does not provide details about the prompts or evaluation setup used for the LLM.

guidelines.notes: Detailed MQM framework guidelines provided: score 0 for no errors, -1 for minor errors, -5 for major errors that impact comprehension/usage, with error type and severity annotations within specific spans.

sample_size.total_generated: multiple datasets across 6 language pairs (EN-DE, ZH-EN, HE-EN, EN-RU, EN-FR, EN-PT-BR)
sample_size.validated_by_both: WMT23 EN-DE dataset with subgroup analysis (HQ-ZERO translations)
sample_size.notes: Analysis includes subsampling to match sample sizes across configurations, with specific focus on HQ-ZERO (zero MQM score) translations

quantitative_scores.notes: Highest F1 score across all language pairs for EN-DE
For EN-DE: trades off with recall
For EN-DE: high recall relative to other metrics

correlation_interpretation.interpretation: low-to-fair correlation, poor correlation for HQ translations

validation_results.summary_finding: GEMBA-MQM (GPT-4 based) achieves the highest F1 score for detecting error-free translations but shows preference bias towards GPT-4 outputs, while automatic metrics overall correlate poorly with human judgments especially for high-quality translations from the same source.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM (GEMBA-MQM) and human evaluators use the same MQM-based criteria for evaluating translation quality and error detection, focusing primarily on identifying high-quality translations with zero or minor errors only.
